breaking.headline: GDP jumps to 4.3% as core PCE runs hot at 3.3%
breaking.fact: The economy grew at a 4.3% annualized rate in Q3, revised up sharply from 3.4%, while October core PCE inflation hit 3.3% year over year — above the 3.2% expected and the highest since November 2023. Markets now price a December Fed hike as nearly certain.

breaking.headline: Selloff deepens after the data — Nasdaq down 4%+, VIX tops 33
breaking.fact: The Nasdaq is down more than 4% and the S&P 500 nearly 3% in morning trading, with the Dow off about 1.6%, as the AI rout resumes after the hot inflation data. The VIX has jumped above 33 and gold is sliding to a 14-month low.

breaking.headline: Bitcoin slides below $60,000, headed for an eighth straight weekly loss
breaking.fact: Bitcoin is trading around $59,300 after briefly touching $64,000 in Monday’s Huang rally, with U.S. spot ETF outflows near $4.9 billion in November and a fresh 2026 low of about $55,250 hit on Saturday.

breaking.headline: Anthropic sinks further below its IPO price as the AI rout spreads
breaking.fact: Anthropic is down again to about $80, further under its $83 IPO price, as the chip-led selloff hits AI names across the board. The stock has fallen every session since its debut last week.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide is trading at €188.88 in Paris, worth $206.54 at the ECB's Nov 25 reference rate of 1.0935, a quiet gain while U.S. tech craters. The industrial-gas giant's defensive profile is doing its usual work on a risk-off morning, with the dollar price tracking the euro near the top of its range. No company news today; watch whether the euro holds above 1.09 into the close.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic slid again to $79.58, now more than 4% below its $83 IPO price as the AI rout deepens. The stock has fallen every session since its debut as investors question whether debt-fueled AI spending will pay off, and today's hot core PCE reading gives the Fed cover to hike. Sean's IPO allocation is underwater, but this is a long-term hold. Watch for a reclaim of $83.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: BIL edged up to $91.63 as Treasury bills keep paying: the distribution yield sits at 4.04% with the last payout of $0.30849 per share paid Nov 5. In a morning when stocks are falling 2-4%, the fund's near-cash profile is exactly why Sean holds it as the portfolio's anchor. It will keep inching higher a few cents a month. Watch the December Fed decision for the yield path.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet plunged 5.2% to $264.49 as the AI selloff spread from chips to the hyperscalers, erasing Monday's rebound and then some. Hot October core PCE at 3.3% hardened bets on a December Fed hike, lifting the discount rate on growth names. GOOGL remains one of Sean's core long-term winners despite the drawdown. Watch whether it holds $260 into the Thanksgiving break. Trading thins into the early close.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly fell 2.1% to $1,378.22, caught in the broad risk-off wave despite no company news. The drugmaker had rallied 3.2% Tuesday and remains well above its recent lows, with its diabetes and weight-loss franchises still the growth engine. Today's drop looks like de-risking ahead of the holiday, not a thesis change. Watch for buyers to step back in after Thanksgiving.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere rose 0.8% to $298.24, one of the few green names as energy rallied on the Hormuz mine strikes and the Houthi claim on Ras Tanura. Brent jumped toward $93 and WTI past $83, lifting LNG exporters with it. Cheniere's long-term contracts insulate it from spot swings, but the tape favors energy today. Watch the OPEC+ meeting Sunday for the next supply signal. U.S. LNG exports stay in strong demand.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia tumbled 8.2% to $142.62, leading the chip rout as Monday's Huang-reinstatement rally fully unwound. Hot core PCE cemented a December hike, and tariff headlines added to the AI-spending doubt that has dogged the sector all month. Sean's call stands: a long-term hold until the probes shake out. The Dec 1 House testimony is the next checkpoint to watch. The board's independent probe remains open.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer slipped 0.5% to $28.32, holding up far better than the growth names as investors rotated toward defensives. The dividend payer had jumped 3.9% Tuesday and stays near the top of its recent range, with its yield cushioning the tape. Sean's gate sits under $32 at 794 shares, so no action here. Watch for any pipeline or guidance news into year-end. The dividend yield above 6% keeps income buyers patient.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab dropped 7.4% to $42.56 as speculative growth names bore the brunt of the selloff. The space stock has given back much of its autumn run in the November risk-off wave, with no company news behind today's slide. Sean holds it as an aggressive-growth bet, so sharp swings are part of the deal. Watch whether $40 holds as support into the holiday. Volatility has been the norm all November.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital rose 0.9% to $8.75, a rare green chip as mortgage REITs benefited from falling Treasury yields. The 10-year slipped to 4.81% after the data, easing pressure on Rithm's book and its dividend story. The stock has climbed steadily off its lows this month. Watch the December Fed decision, which sets the tone for mortgage spreads. Spreads have been friendlier as the 10-year eases.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: The SPAC recovery fund fell 7.5% to $116.36, its worst day in the current slide as de-SPAC names sold off indiscriminately. The fund tracks former SPACs, the market's most sentiment-sensitive corner, and today's risk-off tape hit it hard. It remains an aggressive-growth holding for Sean. Watch for any stabilization once the Thanksgiving break resets sentiment. De-SPAC names have lagged the market all month.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist slipped 0.6% to $47.20, a modest dip as banks held up better than tech in the selloff. The regional lender benefits from a steeper curve and steady credit, and its dividend keeps income investors patient. Today's move is mostly tape-driven, not Truist-specific. Watch the December Fed hike decision and any loan-growth commentary. Regional banks have held up better than tech all month.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony fell 8.0% to $2.01, giving back last week's bounce as the uranium and critical-miner complex sold off with everything else. The stock had re-armed the bottom watch off its lows, but today's tape overwhelmed the story. Antimony's DOD and supply-chain case is unchanged. Watch whether $2.00 holds; a close under it would test the bottom-watch thesis. The bottom watch stays armed.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy dropped 6.2% to $5.23 as uranium names joined the broad selloff, erasing last week's bounce off the $5.30 low. The long-term nuclear story — reactor restarts, SMR approvals, government buying — is intact, but the tape is punishing speculative names. Sean wants to add while prices are low. Watch for a hold above $5.00 into the holiday. Uranium's long-term contracting story is unchanged.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero fell 2.5% to $316.52 even as crude rallied, with refiners lagging the oil move as the market frets over margins and demand. Brent near $93 would normally lift the complex, but today's risk-off tape hit the whole energy patch except the producers. Valero remains a locked long-term hold for Sean. Watch crack spreads and the OPEC+ decision Sunday. Refining margins will set the tone into year-end.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard Target Retirement 2035 held at $28.43, its Nov 24 NAV, with no new price until tonight's close. The balanced fund's bond sleeve cushioned today's equity slide, doing exactly what a target-date fund is built to do. Sean holds it as a steady core position, not a trading vehicle. Watch tonight's NAV for the full read on the selloff. The fund rebalances itself; no action is needed.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: The S&P 500-anchored estimate fell 2.8% to $143.93 as the index slid below 7,000 in morning trading. The estimate tracks the S&P 500 from the $155.58 anchor set Nov 3, so it mirrors the market's drop almost exactly. It remains a work-related holding Sean cannot trade. Watch whether the index can reclaim 7,000 before the early close. The anchor math updates with every S&P close.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: Schwab's money fund holds at $1.00 with a 7-day yield of 3.78%, published Nov 24. The sweep vehicle keeps earning while stocks fall, and per Sean's plan any balance over $1,000 in an account gets sold for a CD. The position should keep evaporating over time. Watch the December Fed hike, which would nudge the yield higher. Any hike flows straight through to money funds.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Treasury money fund holds at $1.00 with a 7-day SEC yield of 4.04%, published Nov 24. It remains the top-yielding cash parking spot in the lineup, beating SWVXX by 26 basis points, and the home for Sean's Treasury cash at eTrade. The yield tracks the Fed's path closely. Watch the December hike decision for the next move. Treasury-bill yields set the pace for money funds.

weekInBrief.headline: Gold slides to a 14-month low as the dollar firms
weekInBrief.body: Gold futures fell about 2.6% to near $3,470 an ounce, the lowest in 14 months, after the strong GDP revision and hot core PCE reading lifted the dollar and cemented December hike bets. Silver fell harder, off nearly 3% toward $40.

weekInBrief.headline: Oil rallies as Hormuz mine strikes revive supply fears
weekInBrief.body: Brent jumped toward $93 a barrel and WTI past $83, reversing the slide on surplus fears, after two more tankers hit mines in the Strait and Houthi claims of a strike on Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura refinery rattled the market. The rally sets up a tense OPEC+ meeting on Sunday.

weekInBrief.headline: Durable goods rise just 0.2% as business spending cools
weekInBrief.body: October durable-goods orders grew 0.2% month on month, well short of the 1.1% economists expected, in the same 8:30 AM data flurry as the GDP revision and PCE report. The miss points to softer business investment heading into year-end.

weekInBrief.headline: OPEC+ gathers Sunday with the market split on output
weekInBrief.body: OPEC+ meets on Sunday, Nov 29, caught between forecasts of a growing global supply surplus and the fresh Hormuz supply risk that has lifted Brent back above $90. Traders expect the group to hold output steady, but the strait standoff gives the hawks fresh ammunition.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Iran’s army said Wednesday it has deployed new surveillance systems and upgraded existing ones to tighten control of the strait, warning vessels that pass without coordinating with Iranian forces face greater risk. The UK maritime authority confirmed three commercial vessels were hit by projectiles on Tuesday, though the damage did not compromise their seaworthiness. Tehran is still demanding the U.S. naval blockade be lifted before it restores normal shipping, offering to reopen the waterway within 48 hours if Washington meets its conditions. Iranian crude exports remain near zero — Kpler puts 40 to 50 million barrels of Iranian oil still on the water in Asia, discharging in China at close to 1 million barrels a day — while non-Iranian Gulf oil keeps flowing at roughly 70% of pre-war volumes.

space.headline: Hubble views an ocean of stars in groundwork for Roman
space.body: Hubble has imaged a densely packed patch of the Milky Way’s galactic bulge, resolving individual stars in a rainbow of colors, as a legacy survey to help researchers interpret upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope observations of the same crowded region. The work will sharpen the hunt for exoplanets, black holes and neutron stars in the bulge.

space.headline: Eruption redraws Iwo Jima’s shoreline with new land
space.body: A volcanic eruption just off the southeast shore of Iwo Jima has extended the Pacific island’s beach, reshaping the coast in satellite views captured by NASA’s Earth Observatory. The eruption is the latest in a series that has steadily added land to the island in recent years.

space.headline: Surplus renewable power could become an industrial resource
space.body: MIT and Georgia Tech researchers report in Joule that future U.S. power systems running on 80% renewables could generate up to about 10% more electricity than can be used or stored at times — and that surplus could be put to work in flexible industrial processes instead of being curtailed.

space.headline: TESS finds eleven new worlds beyond Neptune
space.body: A blind search through eight years of images from NASA’s TESS exoplanet hunter has turned up eleven previously unknown trans-Neptunian objects, circling the Sun 25 to 57 times farther out than Earth, plus eight more candidates awaiting confirmation. The largest may be nearly 1,000 km across.

apod.title: Georgia’s Pecan Belt
apod.credit: NASA Earth Observatory — images by Lauren Dauphin, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey
apod.explanation: Landsat 8 captured this view of pecan orchards clustered along the Flint River near Albany, Georgia, on October 23, 2026, in the middle of harvest season. Georgia has led the nation in pecan production since the 1950s, topping 100 million pounds a year in each of the past three years — and the nuts on Thanksgiving tables across the U.S. likely started in groves like these.
